title: Characterizing and Optimizing LLM Inference Workloads on CPU-GPU Coupled Architectures
summary_zh: 在三種 CPU-GPU 耦合範式 (loosely-coupled PCIe、closely-coupled NVLink-C2C、tightly-coupled on-package) 上對 LLM 推理進行 trace-driven 特徵分析。引入 SKIP profiler 構造 operator-kernel 依賴圖，並以 TKLQT (Total Kernel Launch and Queuing Time) 將工作負載分類為 CPU-bound 或 GPU-bound。發現 GH200 對 Llama-3.2-1B 大 batch prefill 比 LC 平台快 1.9–2.7×，但 GH200 維持 CPU-bound 區間達 LC 的 4×，encoder-only 模型於 GH200 上之 CPU-bound 程度為 LC 的 4 倍。基於 proximity score 的 kernel-fusion 推薦在 CPU-bound 區間提供高達 2.7× (GPT-2) 與 6.8× (XLM-RoBERTa) 的理想化 speedup。
summary_en: Trace-driven characterization of LLM inference across three CPU-GPU coupling paradigms — loosely-coupled (PCIe), closely-coupled (NVLink-C2C), and tightly-coupled (on-package). Introduces SKIP, a PyTorch profiler that builds an operator-kernel dependency graph from CUPTI events, and TKLQT (Total Kernel Launch and Queuing Time) as a fine-grained PU-boundedness classifier. Closely-coupled GH200 outperforms LC platforms by 1.9–2.7× on Llama-3.2-1B prefill at large batch sizes, but remains CPU-bound across a 4× wider batch range, with encoder-only models 4× more CPU-bound on GH200 than on LC. A proximity-score kernel-fusion recommender yields idealised speedups of up to 2.7× (GPT-2) and 6.8× (XLM-RoBERTa-Base) in the CPU-bound region.
